en: Do not let him reach this Beijing;
Repel him and guard the people!
If you are fierce, if you are a hero,
If you are Khan Kongurbay,
We will look to you as our protector.
If you are a timid boy who flees,
We will ride you as a black donkey!
Keep the people in mind,
Keep your eye upon the watch.
A grievous, difficult day has come;
Protect us from it.
To Chin-Machin and Beijing,
Become a true father!
You are my hope, you are my support.
Offering firm resistance to the Burut,
You are my lion who will face him.
Ah, my colt, Kongurbay,
Choose the giants from the governors.
Do not let the vast people be slaughtered;
Keep watch over this Beijing!
Hero Kongurbay, great grim-looking one,
I will agree to what you say.
Of this Chinese people of forty clans,
I will give you one khanate.
Hear what I say.
They are a people mighty in battle;
Take the khanship of the monks!”
Khan Esenkan said this,
Making his worth known to the people.
His arm guards spread broad,
Upon hero Kongur's head
He placed the monks' gemstone badge.
The monks' stone suited him;
He made him a house built on the upland.
“Of Chin-Machin and Kakan,
Ah, my colt, Kongurbay,
Watch closely and scout the roads,” he said.
“From the fierce-wrathed blood-drinker,
From the deceiver who left Altay,
If you have the means, Kongurbay,
Free and rescue us,” he said.
Clothing him in a coat no shot could pierce,
Esenkan was a mighty lord.
Making Manas's circumstances known,
He advanced his counsel far.
The suspected road where Manas would come,
He had Kongurbay block.
Six thousand Chinese, countless governors,
Their chief was Kongurbay.
On the nearer side of him,
Born in Manguba,
Upon all the world,
He had brought extraordinary uproar.
He had speech no human knew;
He had a single eye in his head.
He spared no soul he fought.
The meat of a single pig
Could not fill him at one meal.
If you looked at his nose,
Its shape and appearance,
The nostril of his nose
Was like an uncovered storage pit.
The black brow above his eye
Was like salt ground trampled by livestock.
He would eat those he encountered.
Kakan-Chin's wrestler
Was called Maamytbek the One-Eyed.
He would unleash a fierce fury.
